content.title: About
content.content: Corned beef patty is a ready‑to‑eat beef patty that has been cured in a seasoned brine. It has a firm texture, a rich meaty flavor and a slightly salty aroma typical of traditional corned beef.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional corned beef is cured in a brine with nitrites that preserve its pink color.
Patty format is convenient for quick meals – just heat on a pan or in the microwave.
In the United States corned beef is often served as a sandwich with sauerkraut and mustard.
The brine may contain mustard, cloves, bay leaf and brown sugar.
Beef patty retains most of the protein and iron found in whole meat.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Corned beef patty provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The patty contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as it supplies protein without significant carbs.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc in beef supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The brine makes the patty fairly salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Nitrites
items.content: Some recipes use nitrites to preserve color; excess intake may be undesirable.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to beef.

items.title: Potential bacterial contamination
items.content: As with any meat product, proper storage and thorough cooking are required.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the patty in a skillet, oven or microwave. It is often served in a sandwich with bread, sauerkraut and mustard, or diced for salads and quick‑cook dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the patty refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C in its original packaging. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Ensure the product is fully heated before eating.
